summary: Phelan sprawls across sixty square miles of high desert at roughly 4,500 feet elevation on the northern slope of the San Gabriel Mountains, which means its 301 people per square mile aren't packed into subdivisions — they're scattered across open, scrubby terrain with Joshua trees and wide-angle views of the Mojave. That scale matters: the home-value-to-income ratio sits around 4.3, remarkably accessible compared to most of Southern California, though the tradeoff is distance — the commute down the Cajon Pass on State Route 138 to the Inland Empire job centers in San Bernardino and Victorville can be steep, winding, and weather-dependent, making this functionally a bedroom community for logistics, warehousing, healthcare, and public-sector jobs concentrated along the I-15 corridor below. With nearly 10.7 hours of sunshine daily on average and highs around 72°F, the climate reads as perpetually mild on paper, but high desert means real temperature swings — summer afternoons can push past 100°F while winter nights dip below freezing. There's no walkable downtown, no concentrated restaurant row; grocery and dining options are sparse, separated by long stretches of two-lane road. Phelan is essentially a place where affordable acreage and enormous sky come at the cost of driving for almost everything.
